nodes.recap: chapter header - walking south from Ayonn
nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 15          |
-------------------------------


$CAyonn is behind you.#

The road south is unpaved and wide and empty, and the first day
you walk it in almost complete silence, the weight of the city
still sitting in your chest.# The real sky above, Ayonn's real sky,
without the golden shimmer, is pale and ordinary and
extraordinarily welcome.##

Smiurl walks with his face tilted upward at regular intervals,
checking that the sky is still real.# You notice this, and you do not comment,
because you have been doing the same thing.##

nodes.recap: days of travel south through the southern labyrinths
nodes.text:
The land south of Ayonn is cut through by long canyon passages,
the southern labyrinths: deep-walled gullies of pale rock
that channel the wind and swallow sound and make the days feel both faster
and smaller than they are.##

You cover ground.# The party moves efficiently, automatically,
the rhythms of travel long since internalized.# Corolla reads the
distances with easy competence, Theo sets the pace,
and Efeliah walks and listens, as she always does, to things
you cannot hear.##

Smiurl has not yet recovered from the discovery that south means sea.##

nodes.recap: marching through canyon - Smiurl asks the distance

dialogues.precomment:
You are deep in one of the canyon passages, the walls close on either side,
when Smiurl falls into step beside you and asks the question
that has evidently been troubling him for some time.
dialogues.line: But how long must we walk?# Before the sea, I mean.
dialogues.comment: He says 'the sea' the way a man might say 'the executioner's block.'

dialogues.line: I don't know exactly.# Not long, I think.

dialogues.precomment: Corolla, walking ahead, does not turn around.
dialogues.line:
The distance from here to the coast is about the same as from Ayonn to Seer's Rock.#
A little more, perhaps.# It's just past what you can see at the horizon.
dialogues.comment: She says it the way she says practical things: quickly, without weight, moving on.

dialogues.precomment:
You look at the back of her head.# Something in the way she said it,
the precision of it, the ease, catches your attention.
dialogues.line: How do you know that?# Did your Horde reach that far?
dialogues.comment:
It is an innocent question.# You say it easily, curious, the way you might ask
someone how they know a shortcut.##

Corolla stops walking.##

nodes.recap: Corolla darkens - Kriss pushes - she EXPLODES
nodes.text:
She stops, and for a moment she does not turn around.##

When she does, her expression has changed.# Something has closed
behind her eyes, something that was not there a moment ago,
and she looks at you with a flatness you have not seen from her before.##

$R"It's just a detail."$C#

She turns back to the path and starts walking again.##

Efeliah, a half-step behind you, does not speak.#
You glance at her.# She gives you a look that is neither warning nor encouragement,
only a very slight, almost imperceptible stillness.##

You look at Corolla's back, at the set of her shoulders, and you try to leave it.
But there was something in the way she went quiet, and you cannot.##

$c<<She is hiding something.# I can see it from here.#
I should probably let this go.>>#

$C$R"There's something wrong, isn't there?"$C# you say.##

$R"No, nothing,"$C# she says, without turning around, her voice flat.##

Theo, walking ahead at the front, turns his head a few degrees, just enough
to look sideways with the corner of his eye.# Then he turns back to the path.##

$R"Come on,"$C# you say.# $R"It's obvious you're hiding something."$C##

She stops.##

She turns.##

$R"Leave me alone!"$C##

The cry hits the canyon walls and comes back at you.#
$RLeave me alone$C...# and again, fainter,# $Rleave me alone$C...#
and again, a whisper, fading into the rock.##

Nobody moves.# Smiurl has gone an immediate, shocked gray.#
Efeliah is very still.# Theo does not turn around.##

Corolla's eyes are bright with something you were not expecting,
a fury that has tears at the very edge of it, and she holds your gaze
for one burning moment, long enough for you to feel the full weight
of having accidentally put your hand on something,
before she turns away with a sharp motion of her whole body
and strides ahead, disappearing around the next bend in the canyon.##

You look at Efeliah.# She looks back at you, stricken in her quiet way.#
You look at Theo.##

$B"Come. It'll be dark in a few hours."$C##

You walk.# For the rest of the day you do not see Corolla except as
a distant shape ahead of you, never within speaking distance,
and Smiurl does not make a single sound.##

nodes.recap: evening camp in the canyon - Corolla's absence
nodes.text:
They find a natural clearing where the canyon widens
around a junction of three gullies, old stones arranged in a circle
for a fire: the remnant of someone else's camp, long ago.##

Theo makes the fire without ceremony.# Corolla is already there
when you arrive, sitting at the far edge of the firelight with her back
partly to the group, tending to her pack.# She does not speak,
and nobody speaks to her.##

You cook the meat from the Ayonn stores in silence.#
Efeliah sits with her eyes half-closed, and you are not sure if she is
listening to anyone's thoughts or simply doing them the courtesy
of not listening.# Smiurl eats very quietly, which is not a thing
he does naturally, and the effort of it is visible.##

The fire settles.# Night comes in from the canyon walls above.##

Nobody seems to want to sleep.# Nobody seems to want to speak.##

And then Theo speaks.##

nodes.recap: Theo opens the Øder backstory - Corolla joins mid-telling

dialogues.precomment:
He does not look up from the fire.# His voice is low, and even,
and carries the weight of something that has not been said for a long time.
dialogues.line: It's time we told you our story.
dialogues.comment: You look at him.# Then at Corolla, who has gone very still at the edge of the firelight.

dialogues.precomment:
He looks at the fire, not at you.#
He speaks the way he does everything: steadily, without decoration,
putting one word after the next the way you put one foot after another
when there is no other option.
dialogues.line:
I was born in the city of Øder.# Alone on the mountain range of the same name.#
Corolla is from that city too.# But there is a great difference between us.#
I am the son of laborers.# Mountain workers, for generations.
My people knew nothing but hard work.# They were born for it.#
They loved the mountains above all things.
dialogues.comment:
He says it without sentiment.#
But you hear what is underneath it, as you hear most things underneath Theo's words:
the size of what he is describing by not describing it.

dialogues.line:
She is a noble.# The last of Øder.# Firstborn of the king,
and heir to the throne by right.# She was loved by the people.#
Intelligent and beautiful, and she had no shortage of suitors.#
Naturally she chose none of them.# There were no others of equal rank.#
She would have been the queen of Øder.##

Probably the best ruler the city had ever had.
dialogues.comment:
He stops.# The fire settles.##

Smiurl's skin is a deep, motionless amber, not his anxious amber
but something deeper, older, as if his light has gone still.##

dialogues.line:
But none of that would come to pass.##

Øder had never known war.# High and alone, it was avoided by the Hordes
that had long since spread like a sickness through the colonies of Noi-Hert.
So when they came, we were taken by surprise.# The Horde attacked without warning.#
It was a massacre.# They were many, but by the end of the battle
they were reduced to a few dozen.##

I was taken prisoner, for my usefulness.# I killed two dozen of them first.#
They wanted to persuade me to join them.# I would have died before accepting.#
But something changed my mind.
dialogues.comment:
He looks at the fire.# He does not say what that something was.##

And then a voice from the edge of the light.##

dialogues.precomment:
She has moved without sound.# You did not hear her cross the camp.
She is sitting now within the warmth of the fire, not quite beside anyone,
but present, her arms around her knees, her eyes on the ground.
When she speaks her voice is flat, and absolutely level,
and it costs her something you cannot fully see.
dialogues.line:
We barricaded ourselves in the royal palace, me and the servants,
practically the only survivors.# A hundred and forty people:
cooks, attendants, guards, people who had lived there their whole lives.##

The palace held most of Øder's treasures.# That was what the Horde wanted.
Reduced to less than half their number, they couldn't besiege us.#
So I proposed an exchange.# The freedom of the servants and the prisoners
for the royal treasury.# They accepted.
dialogues.comment: She stops.# Her throat moves.

dialogues.line:
They had the impudence to try to climb the palace walls to take more
before the deal was done.# They hadn't counted on me.#
All the royal line is trained in combat, mind and body both.#
Those crude men were no match for me.##

They freed the servants.
dialogues.comment: She says it simply.# Then:

dialogues.line:
I watched them go.# And then there was nothing left of Øder.#
Great fires were climbing the mountains, lighting the peaks with a ghostly glow,
like an enormous wound.##

My father had been among the first to fall in battle.
dialogues.comment:
The words are flat.# Completely controlled.#
Every muscle in her face is doing something.##

dialogues.line:
I had no home left.# No throne.#
I looked around, and the Horde's chief was standing behind me,
watching me with a grin, and he described, without the least mercy,
exactly what my situation was, and then he invited me to join them.##

I had no other choice.# Where would I have gone?#
I couldn't scatter myself among that handful of servants and butlers.#
I saw Theo.# So I accepted, swearing in the bottom of my heart
that I would make them pay for it, the Horde and its chief.
dialogues.comment: She says the last sentence as if she is still deciding how to feel about it.##

dialogues.line:
We rode with them for years.# Fought beside them, ate with them,
waited for the Chief to make a mistake.##

He did not make mistakes.# He was many things, but not careless.##

And then the canyon happened, and he died,
and it had nothing to do with us.
dialogues.comment: She looks at the fire.# Not at you.

dialogues.line: Is that why you helped me?# At the beginning?
dialogues.comment: You say it quietly.

dialogues.line: No.
We helped you because it was right.
dialogues.comment: He says it from across the fire, his voice unchanged.

dialogues.line:
The Horde met its fate regardless of you.#
They paid, every last one of them who remained, and especially the Chief.#
He wasn't particularly surprised to see us there, at the end.#
He'll have thought we arranged the ambush.
dialogues.comment:
The ghost of something crosses her face.# Not a smile, something older, and very tired.#

$c<<She waited years.# She gave them everything she had left
and rode beside the man who killed her father, and waited,
and when it finally ended it was someone else who ended it.#
Not her.>>#

$CYou do not say anything.# There is nothing to say.##

dialogues.precomment:
A long silence.# The fire pops, and somewhere in the canyon
something moves in the dark, once, and then is still.##

Corolla picks up a small stone and turns it in her fingers.
When she speaks again her voice has changed.# It is quieter,
somewhere further back inside herself.
dialogues.line:
When I was a child, every afternoon I went to my father's study.#
He would sit me on his knee, and let me play with his things.##

The thing I loved most was an old globe of Noi-Hert.#
I would choose a spot at random, pointing with my finger,
and my father would invent a fairy tale about that place, improvising...
dialogues.comment:
Her voice drops.# Falls away entirely.##

You do not move.# None of you do.##

You look at Efeliah.##

She is crying.# Silently, her head down, tears falling freely,
not with any drama, just the quiet fact of it, impossible to look away from.##

dialogues.precomment: You look at Corolla.# She is looking at the stone in her hand.
dialogues.line: I'm sorry.# I... I didn't know.
You couldn't have.
dialogues.comment:
She says it without looking up.# She tries to smile, or something close to it.##

The fire burns low.# Nobody says anything for a long time.##

Smiurl crosses without a word and sits down directly beside Corolla,
close enough that his shoulder is against her arm.# He does not speak.
After a moment his skin shifts from its motionless amber to something warmer:
a slow, steady glow, like firelight from inside.##

Corolla does not look at him.# But she stops turning the stone in her fingers,
and she is still.

nodes.recap: aftermath - silence, everyone settling for the night
nodes.text:
The fire settles.##

Nobody speaks for a long time.# The canyon walls breathe and click,
and somewhere distant something calls once and then is quiet.##

Efeliah dries her face without fuss and takes her food
from the pot without looking up, her eyes soft and distant.#
Theo watches the dark beyond the fire's reach with the usual absolute patience.##

You eat.# The fire burns down.##

Before sleep, in the low last glow of the embers,
you look at the sword planted in the ground at your side,
the Chief's sword, yours now, its metal throwing back a dull red.
Corolla was right.# The most fitting symbol of his defeat.##

nodes.recap: morning - Corolla tells Kriss don't make it strange

dialogues.precomment:
In the morning, before the others are fully awake,
Corolla is already at the edge of the camp rolling her pack.#
You bring her water from the skin, and she takes it without turning around.##

For a moment you stand there, not sure what to say.
dialogues.line: Don't.
dialogues.comment: Her voice is even.# Completely herself again.

dialogues.line: Don't what?
dialogues.comment:
She does turn now.# And her expression is the one you know:#
the clear, slightly sardonic Corolla-gaze that has been reading
you accurately since the day you met.

dialogues.line:
Don't let it make you strange around me.#
Don't look at me differently, don't be careful.##

You asked, I told you.# That is all it is.
dialogues.comment: A pause.# Her eyes hold yours steadily.

dialogues.line:
What I told you last night: that is not who I am now.#
It is why I am who I am now.# There is a difference.
dialogues.comment:
She ties off her pack and stands.##

Behind you, Smiurl has woken up and is already complaining about his back,
Theo is putting out the fire, and the morning is gray and cool
and smells of earth and distant water.##

Corolla brushes past you.#

$R"Come on.# We're losing daylight."$C##

nodes.recap: leaving the labyrinths - the great plain, sea in the distance
nodes.text:
The canyon walls fall back the next morning, and the world opens.##

You step out of the last gully into a vast plain that slopes gently downward
for as far as you can see, and for the first time since you arrived on Noi-Hert
the landscape in front of you is $Wnot$C barren.# Great meadows stretch ahead,
real grass, and further out, at the edges of sight, the dark shapes of trees.##

You run.##

You do it without thinking, without deciding to, just breaking into a run
because the ground is flat and green and the sun is warm and the wind
is coming up from the south, and you run until you reach the top
of a low hill and stop there, breathing hard, with your arms out.#
There is only the warmth of the sun and the voice of the wind.#
For a moment you feel like part of the planet.##

You hear the others catching up behind you.#
You feel Efeliah's mental presence, and something else: a faint, sourceless unease
just at the edge of your perception, a shadow without a shape.##

The incantation breaks.# You become Kriss on a hill again, with his companions,
looking south.##

Efeliah reaches you, and her expression is faintly puzzled.#

$g"I still don't understand what generates your unease,"$C# she says quietly as the others arrive.##

$c<<Neither do I.>>#

$CHe says as much.# She considers it.#

$g"I must resign myself to the evidence.# Perhaps only by waiting,
if we are lucky, will we find answers."$C##

You look south.# Down the long green slope, at the edge of the far horizon,
the faintest blue-gray line.# The sea.##

nodes.recap: end of chapter - the sea visible, the coastal town sighted
nodes.text:
Proceeding faster than expected, in the late afternoon
you make camp near a small stand of trees like nothing you have seen on Noi-Hert before:
tall, with a shape almost like conifers, their needles dark in the fading light.##

A couple of kilometers further south a town is visible, crouched in a bay,
abandoned-looking, or nearly so, but several ships ride at anchor in the harbor
in what appears to be reasonable condition, which suggests someone must be
keeping them that way.##

Efeliah looks at it from a distance.# Her expression does not change,
but something in her posture closes.##

Smiurl looks at it too.# Then he looks at the ships.# Then at the town.##

$Y"I have a bad feeling about this."$C##

You say nothing.# You look at the town in the darkening bay,
and you think he may not be wrong.##
